paper.title_en: Nonreciprocal Shapiro steps in Josephson diodes
paper.abstract_en: Various microscopic mechanisms have been proposed for the Josephson diode effect, which are unified phenomenologically within a nonreciprocal resistively and capacitively shunted junction model. We further systematically investigate the dynamical response of these Josephson diodes to radio-frequency AC driving current, focusing in particular on the nonreciprocity of Shapiro steps. We show that the Shapiro step structures encode the information about the underlying diode mechanisms in both overdamped and noised underdamped junctions. In particular, we propose the zero-voltate step center as a fingerprint of different Josephson diode mechanisms in the overdamped regime, which is captured analytically within a harmonic approximation for small AC amplitudes. Our results provides a route to experimentally distinguish different Josephson diode mechanisms, including those with and without time-reversal symmetry breaking.
